A NAS will let you centralize backups (Time Machine/Windows backups and phone syncs), replace juggling an external drive, and give better always-on access.

What to pick/consider now:
- For a beginner with modest needs, a 2-bay NAS is a good, affordable starting point (simpler and more compact). A 4-bay is better if you expect rapid growth or want more flexible RAID options. 
- Prioritize models with strong security features you asked about earlier: device- or volume-level encryption, granular access controls (ACLs), and 2FA.
- Make sure the NAS supports the backup workflows you want (Time Machine, Windows backup, mobile backup apps).

When you might wait:
- If your current storage isn’t causing problems right now and you want to shop for the best price or learn more, waiting for a sale could be reasonable (you mentioned waiting for sales when buying a laptop).
- If you’re unsure about how many drives/bays you’ll need, take a little time to estimate growth so you don’t buy too small.

Practical next steps: if you decide to buy now, choose a beginner-friendly 2-bay model with AES encryption, ACLs and 2FA (the kinds I previously mentioned), pick drives sized for your needs, and set up automated backups for each device.
